hints.content: To translate quadrilateral $ABCD$ by $1$ unit to the right and $6$ units up, we basically translate quadrilateral $ABCD$'s vertices and connect them.

For example, point $\blueD{D(1,-2)}$ is translated to $\greenD{(2,4)}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a quadrilateral having vertices A at one, negative four, B at negative seven, negative two, C at negative five, one, and D at one, negative two. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves one unit right from vertex D and up.six units to a point at two, four.

hints.content:
Doing this for all vertices and connecting them, we get the following mapping:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a quadrilateral having vertices A at one, negative four, B at negative seven, negative two, C at negative five, one, and D at one, negative two. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves one unit right from the four vertices to form the image of a congruent quadrilateral with vertices two, two, two, four, negative four, seven, and negative six, four.

question.content:
**Draw the image of quadrilateral $ABCD$ under a translation by $1$ unit to the right and $6$ units up.**
